edges.effect_quant: Mesothelioma risk remains elevated even after exposure cessation, and systematic reviews show that lower-dose non-occupational exposure does not eliminate risk; it only changes the exposure context.
edges.population: workers or other adults with low-dose but repeated asbestos exposure
edges.mechanism: Biopersistent asbestos fibers lodge in pleural tissue, provoke chronic macrophage activation, and create long-latency genotoxic injury. Because fiber clearance is poor, even lower-dose repeated exposures can contribute to lifetime mesothelioma risk instead of disappearing once contact stops.
edges.summary: The cleanest message is that asbestos-related mesothelioma risk does not simply vanish when exposure is lighter or remote in time. Meta-regression on exposure cessation, non-occupational exposure syntheses, and occupation-specific mesothelioma meta-analyses all point in the same direction: lower-dose exposure may change magnitude, but it does not make the lifetime signal biologically trivial.
edges.caveats: The exact lifetime risk depends on fiber type, cumulative dose, and years since first exposure. This edge should be read as a long-latency lifetime hazard statement, not as a prediction of short-term mesothelioma incidence after brief exposure.
